goal: Fix catastrophic backtracking in `methodBlockRegex` used by the Symfony controller and route scanners, which causes infinite hang when scanning files with many PHP attributes.

in: Replace nested-quantifier regex with a two-step approach in: - `src/presets/symfony/scan/controllers.js` (L46) - `src/presets/symfony/scan/routes.js` (L172)
Extract shared helper to avoid code duplication
out: Changing scan output format or behavior (pure refactor of matching logic)

acceptance_criteria: Pathological input (20+ `#[Route(...)]` without `public function`) completes in <100ms
Existing Symfony scan tests pass unchanged
Scan output for valid controller files is identical before and after

clarifications.a: `((?:\s*#\[...\]\s*)*)*` — nested quantifiers. When `public function` is not found after many `#[...]` attributes, the engine tries exponentially many ways to partition the attribute sequence.

clarifications.q: Why not just fix the character class?
clarifications.a: The Issue suggested `[^\[\]{}]*` but the real problem is the nested `*` quantifiers, not the character class. Splitting into two steps eliminates the structural issue.
